https://www.politico.eu/article/dutch-pm.text: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten sharply criticized Friday the U.S.’s decision to publicly livestream an execution, labeling it “absurd.” “Personally, I find it truly absurd to broadcast a death penalty execution live,” Jetten told reporters at a press conference in The Hague. “I haven’t discussed this with the U.S. myself recently, but I can imagine that if there is contact with them, for instance, at the level of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, we would certainly make our dissatisfaction known,” he added. The U.S. military plans to carry out a public execution for the first time in recent history, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Thursday. Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan, who was convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, is scheduled to be executed on Dec. 3. The Pentagon has said his death will be livestreamed, but has not provided details on which social media platforms would be used, if any. Jetten said social media platforms in Europe have a responsibility to ensure the execution is not broadcast on the continent. Advertisement Advertisement “As far as I’m concerned, it is really up to the social media platforms in Europe to prevent this from being circulated and broadcast on their channels. But I fear it will be impossible to prevent,” he said. Jetten added that if the execution does appear on European social media, there will be “a great number of reports filed,” as violent content must be moderated by social media platforms under European law. “Video-sharing platforms that allow video content displaying scenes of gratuitous violence must use effective age assurance so that children cannot normally see this content,” a spokesperson for the Irish Media Commission told POLITICO. This means platforms can show violent content as long as they ensure it doesn’t reach minors. The media regulator is currently investigating X over possible breaches in online safety rules for failing to carry out proper age checks. The UN has said livestreaming an execution would amount to torture. “The livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture,” the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights told AFP. The body said its statement is in line with previous ones it has released about public executions in Afghanistan and Iran. The European Commission did not immediately respond to POLITICO’s request for comment. This is a developing story. Advertisement Advertisement

Photograph: Arsvom/AFP/Getty Russia Seven sailors missing after drones strike tankers near Romania’s Black Sea coast Nato source says drones came from Russia, while Romania’s president says attacking commercial ships ‘is unacceptable and has to stop’ Jennifer Rankin in Brussels Thu 15 Oct 2026 13.31 EDT First published on Thu 15 Oct 2026 12.57 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Seven sailors are missing after drones struck two tankers near Romania’s Black Sea ⁠coast, setting them ablaze and raising ⁠fresh security concerns on a ​vital shipping route used by Ukraine. A Nato military source told Reuters the drones that had hit the Wine Trader and the Yara J came from Russia . “The drones that caused ⁠the fires on board two tankers inside Romanian territorial waters were of Russian origin,” the source said. Romania’s president, Nicușor Dan, described the situation in the Black Sea as serious. “Commercial ships are being attacked and sunk,” he wrote on X. “Seafarers killed, injured and missing very close to the shores of Romania and Bulgaria . This is unacceptable and it has to stop.” His statement followed a meeting with Bulgaria’s prime minister, Rumen Radev, and Nato’s secretary-general, Mark Rutte, on Thursday, where they agreed “to strengthen our defences in the Black Sea”, Dan said. Rutte said: “Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed.” A Nato official said the issue would be discussed at a meeting of the North Atlantic Council next week. The missing crew were from the Wine Trader, a San Marino-flagged tanker travelling from Tunisia to Romania. All crew on the Yara J, which was struck just inside Romanian waters late on Wednesday, were safe. Similar incidents in recent weeks have raised fears that the zone is becoming another front in Russia’s war on Ukraine . Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones, but declined to say whether Russia was responsible. Romania shares a 614km (381-mile) border with Ukraine, much of it along the Danube. The country has experienced frequent drone incursions since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, including a daytime encroachment last November that led Nato to scramble fighter jets . skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day after newsletter promotion Russia and Ukraine trade strikes as Trump ‘energy ceasefire’ collapses Read more EU leaders were already concerned about drone strikes on merchant ships off the coast of Bulgaria. On Tuesday, drone strikes on two ships off the coast of Bulgaria prompted emergency rescue operations, with 11 crew member from the HS Dignity, a cargo ship sailing under a Guinea-Bissau flag, still missing. On another ship, the Ukrainian-operated Chelsea 3 sailing under a Maltese flag, rescuers evacuated all 15 crew members, with five receiving treatment for minor injuries. The crew reported that the ship’s deck and hull were hit by three aerial drones. “The results of this attack favour Russia. However, we don’t have any solid evidence that the drones are Russians,” Radev said after arriving in Brussels for an EU summit on Thursday. At least 23 sailors have been reported missing or killed after attacks on commercial shipping near the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania in the past 10 days, according to Reuters. Russia has stepped up its bombing campaign on Ukraine’s Black Sea infrastructure, forcing Kyiv to turn to Danube river ports and Black Sea routes off the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria to export its grain, sunflower oil and other products. According to a draft summit declaration, EU leaders will say that attacks against civilian shipping, including “member state-flagged vessels, such as the recent attacks in Bulgaria’s and Romania’s exclusive economic zones in the Black Sea, are unacceptable and constitute a serious violation of international and maritime law”. https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/isr.text: BACK IN ISRAEL: Previously Missing Mother and Daughter Mali and Liel Yahalomi Return After Being Located in Argentina October 7, 2026 7:30 pm One Comment Mali and Liel Yahalomi, the Israeli mother and daughter whose disappearance abroad sparked a search in August, landed at Ben Gurion Airport on Wednesday afternoon aboard a flight from Athens. The pair exited the terminal wearing matching outfits and did not speak with reporters waiting outside. Authorities did not appear to attempt to detain them. Mali, 50, and Liel, 23, were located in Buenos Aires on August 14, approximately a week after their whereabouts became unknown in Vienna, Austria. Israel Police confirmed at the time that the two had been found on an intercity bus in the Argentine capital. The mother and daughter had failed to board their scheduled return flight from Prague, raising concern about their whereabouts. Their travels began with a flight from Israel to Prague, followed by a visit to Vienna. They apparently traveled through Frankfurt before eventually reaching Buenos Aires.
